atoms.text: Misinformation is false or misleading information that is shared as if it were true. It has become a serious problem on social media, where many people read and share information daily. When misinformation spreads, it can confuse people and affect how they understand important topics in their lives.
atoms.sound: Misinformation is false or misleading information that is shared as if it were true. It has become a serious problem on social media, where many people reed and share information daily. When misinformation spreads, it can confuse people and affect how they understand important topics in their lives.

b: ++information that is shared as true but is false or misleading
information that is confusing but based on facts
information that people disagree with online
information that exists online

atoms.a: What can happen when misinformation spreads online?
b: ++People may misunderstand important topics.
People learn new information more easily.
People stop using social media completely.
People will be happier.

atoms.text: Moreover, research shows that misinformation spreads especially fast on social media. One major study found that false stories were 70% more likely to be shared than true stories. Researchers explain that false information often sounds surprising or emotional, which makes people more likely to pass it on. As a result, misinformation can spread widely in a short time.

atoms.a: What does emotional most likely mean in this paragraph?
b: ++causing strong feelings
related to numbers and facts
easy to forget
easy to understand

atoms.a: Why do false stories keep spreading after they are shared?
b: ++They grab people’s attention and trigger strong reactions.
They are always written by experts.
They include long explanations.
They are in video format.

atoms.a: What does this paragraph suggest about how people share information online?
b: ++People sometimes share posts without checking if they are true.
People only share information they fully understand.
People avoid sharing emotional posts.
People always check if what they read online is true.

atoms.text: Misinformation can also affect the choices people make. Studies report that people who believe false information are more likely to make poor decisions, especially about important issues. Research also shows that seeing false information many times can reduce trust in real news. Because of this, misinformation can have serious effects on individuals and communities.

atoms.a: Why might someone make a bad decision after reading false information online?
b: ++They may believe something that is not true.
They want to disagree with others.
They enjoy reading online posts.
They think the topic is not important.

atoms.a: How could seeing false information many times affect a person?
b: ++It may make it harder to know what information to trust.
It helps them learn new facts faster.
It makes them less interested in news.
It makes them more educated.
